title: Instrument lifecycle outcomes and bounded audit reports
summary: Measure whether Matter improves whole episodes while making overhead and uncertainty visible. Metrics must distinguish eligible, delivered, consumed, acted-upon and verified outcomes and must include important cases that stayed quiet.
in_scope: Stable metric definitions, reason codes and bounded tracing.
Episode-level reports, quiet-case sampling and actual cost/latency accounting.
out_of_scope: Deploying or modifying a downstream project as part of this planning ticket without that implementation task.
Treating synthetic checks as evidence of live provider or user outcomes.
implementation: Define event counters and denominators with scope, rule-family and model/config versions.
Aggregate outcomes by independent episode/source groups without treating duplicate reports as independent samples.
Expose compact audit reports that retain missing evidence and unknown consumption rather than requiring manual acknowledgments.

acceptance.criterion: Delivery and verified benefit cannot be conflated in metrics or reports.
acceptance.verification: Replay an episode with delivered-but-unconsumed and consumed-without-verification updates and inspect separate counters.

acceptance.criterion: Suppression cannot appear successful solely because nothing was emitted.
acceptance.verification: Include labeled important quiet cases and verify missed/late outcomes appear in the report denominator.

acceptance.criterion: Reported overhead includes all evaluation, retrieval, retries and delivery blocking work.
acceptance.verification: Compare instrumented event totals with an independently measured episode trace and account for failed calls.

tests: No events collected versus zero errors among collected events.
Repeated observations from one source group.
Budget exhaustion with no human action required.
risks: Optimizing notification count alone can hide missed developments.
Verbose tracing can leak evidence or consume more resources than evaluation.

reuse.application: Preserve the explicit scope, provenance, qualification, and evidence boundaries in the governing contracts.
